titleEn: Lights Across the River Go Out—Bedtime!

pages.text: "I'm not sleeping! One more!" Mina made hand shadows before the lamp. The river outside the window was dark and calm. Mina held back a yawn.
Mom spread the quilt. "Only two lights are left across the river." "I'm not sleepy!" Mina opened another finger, making a new shadow.
But their eyelids grew heavy. A drooping hand blurred the shadow. A big yawn opened their mouth. "Am I a little sleepy?"
Experienced eldest child Raju dragged in a quilt and lay beside Mina. "I'm sleeping. I counted one light left across the river." Mina went to the window.
The village's last light went out. Mina stopped playing and lowered their hands. "Everyone must have gone to bed."
Mom brought the lamp to the window. "Lights Across the River Go Out—Bedtime!" Mina slipped under the quilt. Beside them, Raju slowly closed their eyes.
Mom dimmed the lamp. Six or seven small stars appeared outside, making the room unscary. Her voice was quiet and warm. "Lights Across the River Go Out—Bedtime!"
Mina reached out for one last little shadow. Mom gently held that hand. "The children across the river must be under their quilts now, too." Mina tucked the hand inside.
The next night, Mina watched lights go out one by one. "Mom, I'm going to bed now." Mina pulled up the quilt.
Mom hugged Mina and covered them. "Sleep well." Mina closed their eyes and whispered, "You, too, Mom."
